title: MetaMask Core Perps advanced order types, proven natively on HyperLiquid (TAT-3511)
description: Shipped with the package so any checkout can re-prove the contract. Proves the TAT-3511 acceptance criteria against real HyperLiquid orders through the controller's full signing/provider path — no wrapped evidence. For each advanced order type (stop market, stop limit, take-profit market, take-profit limit, reduce-only, partial TP/SL) the recipe places a REAL order on testnet via metamask.perps.place_order, asserts it is visible in open-orders state with its trigger data round-tripped from the exchange (placement type, trigger price, execution mode, reduce-only flag, partial quantity) via metamask.perps.assert_orders, cancels it via metamask.perps.close_orders, and asserts the final state is empty. Orders rest far from mid and are post-only so they cannot fill during the proof, and the account is converged to flat before and after. Mainnet is exercised too, as a cross-venue regression guard: read-back first, then one explicitly authorized ~$15 reduce-only stop_limit on ETH (a market where this account holds nothing) placed, asserted, and cancelled with REAL funds under CORE_PERPS_ALLOW_MAINNET_WRITES=1. The account's real BTC position-bound TP/SL orders are asserted open before and after, proving the probe touched nothing else. The remaining nodes cover the unit/integration suites, provider-agnostic typing, the package build and emitted declarations, the full test suite, and the changelog.

params_are_provider_agnostic.cmd: cd packages/perps-controller && node -e "var fs=require('fs');var s=fs.readFileSync('src/types/index.ts','utf8');var m=s.slice(s.indexOf('export type OrderParams'), s.indexOf('export type OrderResult'));var vocab=['tpsl','triggerPx','isMarket','normalTpsl','positionTpsl'];var lines=m.split('\n');var offending=lines.filter(function(l){return vocab.some(function(t){return l.indexOf(t)!==-1}) && l.trim().indexOf('grouping?:')!==0 && l.indexOf('tpslLinkage')===-1 && l.trim().indexOf('*')!==0});var groupingIdx=lines.findIndex(function(l){return l.trim().indexOf('grouping?:')===0});var deprecated=groupingIdx>-1 && lines.slice(Math.max(0,groupingIdx-6),groupingIdx).join(' ').indexOf('@deprecated')!==-1;var has=['triggerPrice','takeProfitSize','stopLossSize','reduceOnly','tpslLinkage'].filter(function(t){return m.indexOf(t)!==-1});console.log(JSON.stringify({vocabOutsideGrouping:offending,groupingDeprecated:deprecated,fields:has}))"
params_are_provider_agnostic.intent: AC5 — inspect the OrderParams declaration: no protocol vocabulary outside the one pre-existing `grouping` field, that field carries an @deprecated pointer to the provider-agnostic `tpslLinkage` that replaces it, and the trigger/partial fields are present.

params_no_protocol_leak.intent: AC5 — the only protocol-shaped field in OrderParams is the deprecated `grouping`, which now has a provider-agnostic replacement, so a second provider never has to speak HyperLiquid

params_expose_trigger_fields.intent: AC5 — the placement extension and the TP/SL linkage are expressed in provider-agnostic fields a second provider can map

package_build.intent: AC6 — the emit-producing build, run from the repo root. A package-scoped build uses --no-references and needs sibling packages' dist/index.d.ts, which only the root build produces, so the root build is the reliable node in a shared checkout.

package_build_exit.intent: AC6 — the build succeeds with the widened OrderType and the new exported types

package_build_dist.intent: AC6 — the published type declarations carry the new provider-agnostic option (OrderParams is emitted in dist/types/index.d.cts; the root barrel only re-exports)

full_test_suite.intent: AC6 — the full package suite with coverage thresholds

full_test_suite_exit.intent: AC6 — full suite green, coverage thresholds met

changelog_validate.intent: AC6 — changelog entry present and valid

changelog_documents_types.intent: AC6 — the changelog describes the new placement types for consumers

mainnet_btc_untouched_before.intent: Safety baseline: the account's own BTC position-bound TP/SL orders are open on MAINNET before the probe. The probe deliberately runs on ETH, where this account holds nothing, because close_orders is symbol-scoped — so no real protective order is ever cancelled.

mainnet_place.intent: Mainnet signing validation with REAL funds, explicitly authorized: place one ~$15 reduce-only stop_limit on ETH, 30% below mid and post-only. Reduce-only means it can never open exposure, and it rests far from mid so it cannot fill in the seconds before it is cancelled. Requires CORE_PERPS_ALLOW_MAINNET_WRITES=1.

mainnet_assert_open.intent: AC1/AC2 on MAINNET — the trigger placement is visible in open-orders state with its placement type, limit execution and reduce-only flag round-tripped from the real exchange

mainnet_cancel.intent: AC3 on MAINNET — cancel the probe order through the controller (ETH only)

mainnet_assert_none.intent: AC3 on MAINNET — final state asserted: the probe order is gone

mainnet_btc_untouched_after.intent: Safety proof: the account's real BTC position-bound TP/SL orders are still open on MAINNET after the probe — the mainnet validation touched nothing but its own ETH order
